series: The Dark Side of Once Upon a Time
title: Rumpelstiltskin: The Bargain and the Secret Name
version_scope: Brothers Grimm, final 1857 German edition, as rendered in Margaret Hunt's 1884 English translation. This is one documented literary version, not a claim about the tale's first or only form.

sources.edition: Jacob Grimm and Wilhelm Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, 7th edition (1857), vol. 1, tale 55, Rumpelstilzchen; translated by Margaret Hunt as Grimm's Household Tales, vol. 1 (London: George Bell and Sons, 1884), tale 55, Rumpelstiltskin, pp. 221–225.
sources.scope_note: The linked online transcription is Hunt's English text based on the Grimm tale; the episode identifies the German source edition and translation separately. The 1857 story ends with Rumpelstiltskin stamping his foot into the floor and wrenching it free.

narration: A miller wanted to impress the king, so he made a reckless boast: his daughter could spin straw into gold. That boast would put her life in danger. The king locked her in a room piled with straw. “Make it gold by morning,” he ordered. “Or you die.” Then a tiny stranger appeared. “I can help,” he said. “What will you give me?” She handed over her necklace. By dawn, the straw had become gold. But the king wanted more. The next night, he filled a larger room. The little man returned, and this time he took her ring. On the third night, there was still more straw—and she had nothing left. The king promised to marry her if she succeeded. The stranger demanded her first child. She agreed. The king kept his promise. A year later, the stranger came for the baby. The queen offered riches instead. “No,” he said. He wanted the child. He gave her three days to guess his name. For two days, every guess failed. Her messengers searched the land, but no one knew the answer. On the third day, a messenger returned: he had seen the little man dancing beside a fire at the forest's edge, singing to himself. The queen spoke the name: “Rumpelstiltskin!” Enraged, he stamped his foot so deep into the floor he had to wrench it free. Then he fled. Her child was safe.
